members.text: Accelerating trunk rotation all the way through to the target instead of decelerating short of the target to release the shoulder
The player fails to freeze or decelerate the trunk right before contact, leaking rotational momentum instead of transferring it into the arm.
Trunk spins continuously without an anchor to decelerate, preventing momentum transfer to the arm and racket.
The player twists continuously through contact instead of allowing hip rotation to be transient and brake to create a whip effect.

groups.why_run1: Failing to decelerate or brake trunk rotation before contact, preventing rotational momentum from transferring into the arm and racket.
groups.why_run2: Failing to decelerate or brake trunk rotation before contact, preventing rotational momentum transfer into the arm and racket.

members.text: Pulling too close to the body or relying excessively on rotational body mechanics rather than pulling well out in front.
Catching the ball too late with the pull slot set too close to the stomach rather than out in front.

groups.why_run1: Pulling or making contact too close to the body rather than well out in front.
groups.why_run2: Setting the pull slot or contact point too close to the body instead of extending out in front.

members.text: The player lets the hips drift forward and slides the knee forward over the toes instead of hinging at the hips and keeping the hips behind.
Hips extending forward in front of the shoulders with knees forward and chest up (quad dominant posture) rather than maintaining a hip hinge.

groups.why_run1: Allowing the hips and knees to push forward rather than hinging at the hips.
groups.why_run2: Drifting or extending the hips forward with knees advancing rather than maintaining a stable hip hinge.

members.text: Players grant opponents too much respect on defense and attempt wild bailout shots rather than hitting high, safe balls back into court.
Players believe they must execute miraculous, razor-thin knifing or driving shots under pressure instead of making their opponent beat them.

groups.why_run1: Attempting low-percentage miraculous or bailout shots when under pressure instead of hitting safe, neutral balls to stay in the point.
groups.why_run2: Attempting low-percentage miraculous bailout shots under defensive pressure instead of resetting the point with high, safe balls.

members.text: Conceiving the serve internally as a down-to-up or low-to-high vertical motion prevents the body from loading in the horizontal in-to-out plane.
The player attempts to throw the racket up or down-and-up directly at the ball rather than throwing it out to the hitting side.

groups.why_run1: Swinging or directing the racket vertically up directly at the ball rather than swinging outward along an in-to-out path.
groups.why_run2: Directing the swing path vertically (down-to-up) instead of swinging and releasing outward to the hitting side.
